sources.citation: Okamoto et al. 2025, Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta
Lawal et al. 2026, Geophysical Research Letters
Hao & Li 2018, Frontiers in Earth Science 6:180
sources.supports: Komatiite, peridotite and basalt reacted with H2O-CO2 at 200-500 C; secondary clays/carbonates and gases were measured, directly instantiating a reactive crust-fluid-gas interface.
sources.does_not_establish: Does not by itself demonstrate the full N030 capacity wording, especially catalysis, in one closed chain.

sources.citation: Ueda et al. 2021, Geochemistry Geophysics Geosystems 22:e2021GC009827
sources.supports: Time-resolved hydrothermal experiments on synthetic komatiite and CO2-rich Hadean seawater measured evolving fluid chemistry under 100-350 C conditions, including H2-rich fluids.
sources.does_not_establish: Hydrothermal conditions already impose a reacting water-rock system; source strengthens gradients/chemistry but is not alone a proof of the initial interface bootstrap.

sources.supports: Natural komatiite produced substantially more labelled methane than synthetic komatiite during hydrothermal alteration; catalytic mineral candidates were investigated.
sources.does_not_establish: Catalyst identity was inferred rather than isolated as the unique cause, so this is supporting context rather than a canonical HC02 promotion proof.

next_discriminating_evidence: complete the N030 semantic audit for HC02, especially direct catalytic capacity within the same primitive-crust water/gas interface; if sufficient, promote HC02 rather than rewrite H052
mechanistic_progress: HC02 now gives a source-backed direct bootstrap route N051+N028 -> N030 and closes 53/53 mathematically while leaving H052 unchanged; canonical closure remains 46/53 until semantic promotion criteria are met
